narr: A decaying MCS/MCV moved through the Mid-South during the overnight/early morning hours of May 22. A slow moving cold front was stretched over the Missouri Bootheel and moisture surged northward allowing for plentiful instability. This instability collided with remnant outflow boundaries from previous convection. Peak diurnal heating hours, moisture, and enough lift caused damaging winds, large hail, and flash flooding across West Tennessee.
ev: Over 13 roadways in and around the city of Camden that are inundated with water closed to flash flooding.

Several inches of rainfall (4.24) reported by weather observer in Paris today after showers and thunderstorms. Numerous county roads and streets were flooded around Henry County. Eleven homes had minor flood damage due to flash flooding along creeks.
